# odyssey-083 — review, pass 1 (Odyssey 17.101–203)

Reviewer pass 1. `gloss.json` was not read (pass 2). `t` was not touched: the units' `t`, joined in order, reproduce the packet's 103 lines word for word; every `ln` is the line of the unit's first word; every `\n` in `t` falls on a line end and `l` has one line per line of `t`; `i` has no `\n`. `p` stands on exactly the thirteen units that open a Murray paragraph (17.101, 107, 124, 147, 150, 152, 162, 166, 174, 177, 185, 192, 197). Quotation marks: seven speeches (Penelope 101–104; Telemachus 108–148; Theoclymenus 152–160; Penelope 163–164; Medon 174–176; Eumaeus 185–190; Odysseus 193–195), 7 “ and 7 ” in both layers; Menelaus's speech inside Telemachus's (124–146) takes ‘ … ’, opened at 124 and closed at the end of 17.146. Every speech opens and closes inside this part; the previous part (odyssey-082) ends at 17.100 with Penelope's introductory line, so her speech begins here (see the first change). Scansion: the packet flags none; no hand scan owed, no irregularity note added.

Repeated lines were compared with the published English character for character: 17.107, 129–131, 132–135, 137, 138–141, 143–146 (the `i`/`l` of 145–146), 155–156, 163, 164–165, 192 are identical to the shipped wording; 17.193 (= 16.136, odyssey-078, not in the packet) also matches. 17.159 (`ἀτὰρ μνηστῆρσι κακὸν πάντεσσι φυτεύει`, = a line of odyssey-073) was not in the packet; its `l` was brought to the published wording (below).

**Counts of changes: high 0, medium 16, low 11 (27 rows; each split counts once).**

## Findings considered and refused

| Line | Finding | Reason refused |
|---|---|---|
| 146 | Line 146 lacks final punctuation in Murray's text (drafter). | Real, and kept: the text is exactly Murray's; the unit ends at the paragraph break (147) and the note says so. |
| 124–146 | Drafter merged units "for quote nesting". | Refused as a reason; the units were split at the stops (above). Nested ‘ ’ opens on the first unit of Menelaus's speech and closes on 145–146. |
| 185–187 | σ’ = σε as the subject of λιπέσθαι. | Checked: ἦ σ’ ἂν ἐγώ γε … βουλοίμην … λιπέσθαι is βούλομαι with accusative and infinitive; σοι would leave λιπέσθαι without a subject. Kept; note already says it. |
| 196 | ἦ φατ’ as φατε 'you (people) say'. | Kept; φατ’ cannot be a singular and the plural of general address is the usual reading. The note says so. |
| 196 | οὐδός "threshold" in `l`, "ground" in `i`. | The two layers resolve the word's two senses on purpose (new row; note says "threshold" is the dictionary sense, here probably the ground underfoot). |
| 159 | ἀτάρ should be "but". | odyssey-073 (same half-line) renders it "and"; "and, but" in its note; consistency wins. |
| 195 | "a club cut … to lean on" reads oddly. | The table fixes ῥόπαλον "club"; the drafter's "cudgel" overrode a ratified row. The part follows the table; the question whether an existing row may be varied for a walking-stick is for the owner (to QUESTIONS.md at publish). |

| 109 | `i` drops "both" of ἔς τε … καὶ. | `l` keeps it; `i` is prose. |

## Parses checked and kept (no change)

ᾤχεθ’ (ᾤχετο, τ > θ before ἅμ’ with rough breathing; augment ᾤ-), ᾠχόμεθ’, δάκρυσ’ (δάκρυσι), ἐντυνώμεθα (subj. mid. 1 pl.; pres. and aor. coincide), ἐξερέῃσι (subj. 3 sg. after ὁπότε, hind as subject; the known entry stands), φατ’ (φατέ, 2 pl.; the Greek has no singular form to elide to φατ’), ἥνδανε (known entry stands; the unit note's ἐ + ἁ agrees in effect), μέμβλωκε (perf. of βλώσκω; ἦμαρ subject; the `μάλιστα` broadening is right: "for the most part"), ἀρισφαλέ’ (ἀρισφαλέα, masc. acc. sg. with οὐδόν), ὠτρύνοντ’ (augment ὠ-), σκηρίπτεσθ’, ἕσπερα (neut. pl., acc. after ποτί), ῥίγιον, ῥίγιον's "colder" (kept; the unit says "more chilling"), and the broadened αἰδοίη (voc.), σταθμὸν (steading) and ὄρινε (impf. unaugmented) all fit their lines.
